value.title: A first-class harness hooks verb
value.summary: Mode: Full. harness owns agent-harness hooks: the installer, the runtime the installed hooks call back into, a git commit intercept, and a trace2 tickler that restores attribution a sandbox would otherwise destroy.

sections.name: goals
value: A `harness hooks` verb family that is BOTH the management surface (install/status/uninstall/list) and the runtime the installed hooks invoke (fire) — the config we write points back at harness, so upgrading harness upgrades hook behaviour with no reinstall.
Hooks installed into every agent client harness supports, driven by ONE declarative matrix rather than per-client bespoke code.
A git intercept that detects a genuine new commit and never guesses — a missing note is recoverable, a false one is a confident wrong answer nobody audits.
A trace2 tickler that restores attribution under a sandbox with ZERO changes to the customer machine — no trace2 redirection, no sandbox setting, no security trade.
Doctor installs hooks alongside the pinned git-ai, under the existing safeLayer containment and warn-only exit-0 posture.
Hook actions pluggable, so commit detection is the first action and not the only one.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Fixing the human-absorption case (human lines stamped AI). It was never reproduced here — everything reproduced was TOTAL LOSS — and it is a different defect. Do not describe this plan as fixing it.
Explaining or fixing Claude Code Bash-class tool calls recording nothing on an unsandboxed machine (dossier 7.5). Unexplained, separate, and possibly the real cause of the original complaint.
Changing customer machine configuration — no global trace2 redirection, no Cursor sandbox edits, no writes to ~/.cursor beyond the hook entry we own.
Filing issues upstream to git-ai.
Proving Windows end to end. The named-pipe path is code-portable but unobserved, and verification needs the remote Windows agent.

value.claim: harness hooks fire <agent> --phase post writes a correct line-level note for a commit the daemon never observed, proven against a live daemon with the commit trace2 discarded.

A commit made by a sandboxed agent produces a note whose AGENT-authored line ranges map to the correct agent session. Any `humans` entry is produced by git-ai's own pre-hook, not by us — it is OBSERVED and reported, never asserted as a pass condition. A missing or wrong `humans` entry is recorded as a finding against the declared non-goal, never as a blocker on this plan.

No event is emitted unless the agent AUTHORED the commit here. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE INDEX STATE RECORDED AT PRE — measured, and the only mechanism that works. Three candidates are measured DEAD and must not be relied on: parent-count catches only --no-ff merges; the reflog subject catches ff-pull, cherry-pick, revert and amend; and .git state (MERGE_HEAD/SQUASH_MSG) DOES NOT EXIST when our hook runs — MERGE_HEAD is never written by --squash at all, and SQUASH_MSG is unlinked by git before even git's own post-commit hook fires, so it must not be a classifier parameter. TWO CLASSES MUST BE REJECTED: (a) HEAD did not advance by exactly one — checkout, reset --hard, rebase, amend, no-op, detached HEAD, no prior recorded state, multi-commit ff pull; and (b) HEAD advanced by one whose first parent IS the recorded HEAD but nothing was authored here — the SEVEN MEASURED DEFEATERS merge --squash, cherry-pick -n, revert -n, git apply, checkout REF -- path, restore --source, read-tree -m -u (how git subtree works), plus single-commit ff pull, --no-ff merge, cherry-pick, revert, git am. Class (b) is byte-identical to an authored commit on all three dead mechanisms; at PRE every member has an ALREADY-STAGED index where a genuine agent edit has a CLEAN one. The only permitted error mode is a false NEGATIVE. A human committing inside the PRE/POST bracket is indistinguishable and is an asserted KNOWN-BLIND row, not a gap to close.
harness hooks install is idempotent: a second run leaves every touched config byte-identical.
Installing preserves every pre-existing hook entry in a shared config, including git-ai own entries, and never reformats away content it did not write.
harness hooks status --json reports per-agent state from EVIDENCE (a config file we can show we changed) and never from a claim we cannot verify.
Every hook failure path exits 0 and prints nothing to the agent — a broken harness never breaks the customer editor session.
harness doctor installs hooks alongside the pinned git-ai; any failure is warn-only at exit 0 with every other doctor row still printed.

`HARNESS_NO_HOOKS=1` skips hook installation entirely — honoured by `harness hooks install` ITSELF (Phase 2), not only by doctor's call site, so the opt-out cannot be bypassed by invoking the verb directly.
harness hooks uninstall removes only entries we own and leaves other tools entries intact.

A fire that failed to emit is VISIBLE in `harness hooks status --json` with its cause — proven by a fixture where the socket is unreachable. Exit 0 must never be the only signal; a silent failure is the exact defect this plan exists to fix, and shipping one would reproduce it.

The root README states plainly that `harness doctor` installs the git-ai collector AND installs our agent hooks on first run — what it writes, where, and how to opt out with HARNESS_NO_HOOKS=1. A reader must not be surprised by a machine change they did not know doctor makes.

value.title: The hook runtime — `harness hooks fire`, the commit intercept, and the trace2 tickler
value.brief: Build the mechanism that is already proven, behind ports. `harness hooks fire <agent> --phase pre|post` reads the agent's payload on stdin, records HEAD AND THE INDEX STATE on pre, and on post emits six synthetic trace2 events ONLY when the agent AUTHORED a new commit here. REUSE the EXISTING socket port src/adapters/net/socket-probe-port.ts (plan 074) — do NOT build a second one. Services must never import node:net directly. Every path exits 0 and writes nothing the agent can see; because exit 0 is unconditional it carries no information, so NO assertion may rest on it — assert on the journal. THE GUARD IS THE HARD PART. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE INDEX STATE RECORDED AT PRE — measured, and the only mechanism that works. Three are measured DEAD: parent-count catches only --no-ff merges; the reflog subject catches ff-pull, cherry-pick, revert and amend; and .git state (MERGE_HEAD/SQUASH_MSG) DOES NOT EXIST when our hook runs — MERGE_HEAD is never written by --squash at all and SQUASH_MSG is unlinked before git's own post-commit hook fires, so it must NOT be a classifier parameter (a fabricated input would make a broken system look green). SEVEN transitions are byte-identical to an authored commit on all three: merge --squash, cherry-pick -n, revert -n, git apply, checkout REF -- path, restore --source, read-tree -m -u. At PRE every one has an ALREADY-STAGED index; a genuine agent edit has a CLEAN one. Only error mode is a false NEGATIVE, the direction doctrine demands. A human committing inside the PRE/POST bracket is indistinguishable — an asserted KNOWN-BLIND row, not a gap to close. ALSO in scope: CONCURRENCY — two POSTs racing both read state before either writes; the PRE write must be atomic (exclusive create or lock). BUILD THE SENSORS FIRST: the provocation suite runs against REAL git repositories (a suite that feeds the pure classifier a fabricated state proves only that the implementation matches itself), and the live-daemon note fixture comes before feature code. Prove on macOS AND Linux; Windows stays UNVERIFIED and is handed to the remote agent on #108.

value.title: The installer — one declarative matrix, four write strategies
value.brief: `harness hooks install|status|uninstall|list`, all with `--json`, driven by ONE matrix over four write strategies (JSON merge, plugin file, script file; TOML/Codex deferred). Authoritative design in assets/workshops/hooks-installing.md. `HARNESS_NO_HOOKS=1` is honoured HERE, in the verb itself, so it cannot be bypassed by calling install directly. Fix the four things git-ai gets wrong: take backups, preserve comments and key order, match only an owned marker, and always quote plus normalise the binary path. Uninstall must restore the ORIGINAL bytes. Fixture tests per agent, including a config that already holds git-ai's own hooks.

value.title: Doctor integration, live install on this machine, and docs
value.brief: Doctor installs hooks alongside the pinned git-ai under safeLayer containment, warn-only at exit 0, honouring HARNESS_NO_HOOKS=1, with an evidence-based row. Then INSTALL IT LIVE on this machine into Cursor via our own verb — backing up ~/.cursor/hooks.json first, since it carries both the POC hook and git-ai's own entries — and ship assets/poc/CURSOR-PROMPT-8.md so Jordan can validate the whole chain in one paste. DOCS: the root README must say plainly that `harness doctor` installs the git-ai collector AND our agent hooks on first run — what it writes, where, and how to opt out. That is a machine change on someone else's computer and a user who is surprised by it has been failed, however good the reason. Also docs/how/ and an update to docs/how/telemetry/sandbox-02-workarounds-proven.md, which now understates what we know.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Measured 2026-08-09. Evidence: assets/research-dossier.md (the failure chain, the controlled A/B, five measured dead ends), assets/workshops/hooks-installing.md (the authoritative installer design, from a full read of git-ai's 15 installers), assets/poc/ (16 working artifacts). Controlled A/B in a real sandboxed Cursor session: hook DISABLED produced NO note on a four-file mixed commit; hook ENABLED produced a correct three-way split (cursor / human / claude), with the human's 11 hand-written lines correctly separated. The git-ai install and parse surfaces are byte-identical between our v1.6.21 pin and the v1.6.22 checkout (verified by diff over src/mdm, install_hooks.rs and checkpoint_agent/), so the installer reference applies to the pin with no version caveat.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Cursor's sandbox refuses AF_UNIX connect(), so a sandboxed `git commit` never reaches the git-ai daemon and NO note is written at all — total attribution loss, not misattribution. The hook runner is not sandboxed — MEASURED on macOS; ASSUMED and unverified on Linux and Windows, and the whole design rests on it. This plan makes harness own agent-harness hooks end to end: a `harness hooks` verb family that is BOTH the installer and the runtime the installed hooks call back into, a git intercept that detects a real new commit from HEAD, and a trace2 tickler that tells the daemon a commit happened so it writes the note it would otherwise miss. THE TICKLER changes nothing on the customer machine — no trace2 redirection, no sandbox setting, no security trade. The INSTALLER does write, deliberately: the single hook entry we own, backed up first.

value.approach: Hybrid — real behaviour against a live git-ai daemon for the intercept and the tickler; table-driven fixture tests for the agent matrix and the installer.
value.rationale: The tickler cannot be proven by a fake: the finding IS that the daemon accepts a synthesised stream, so a fake that accepts it proves nothing. The installer is pure file transformation and needs no live anything.
value.focus_areas: Commit-detection edge cases (the dangerous direction); config merge preserving foreign entries byte-identically; comment and key-order preservation; install/uninstall symmetry; idempotency; exit-0 on every failure path; a binary path containing spaces.
value.excluded: Windows end-to-end (no instrument until the remote agent reports); git-ai internals we do not own; Codex TOML trust state (deferred).
value.mock_usage: Targeted only — fake adapters for the fs, git and socket ports per the constitution (fakes over mocks; never vi.mock of internal modules).

value.location: Root README (MUST state that `harness doctor` installs the git-ai collector AND the agent hooks on first run, what is written where, and the HARNESS_NO_HOOKS=1 opt-out), docs/how/ for the mechanism, and an update to docs/how/telemetry/sandbox-02-workarounds-proven.md.
value.rationale: Doctor now changes the user's machine in two ways on first run. A README that does not say so leaves the user to discover it from a diff, which is how trust in an installer dies. The sandbox-02 doc already held a working answer from 2026-08-07 and an evening was spent rediscovering it; leaving it stale guarantees a third rediscovery.

value.question: Idempotency of the emit (dossier 9.1): the POC writes state AFTER emitting so a repeat POST returns early — mitigated in code, unproven by a test. Does a double fire for one commit double-write or corrupt the note?
Staleness ceiling (dossier 9.2): the daemon's reflog cursor must predate the commit. Proven at ~2s. How old can it get before rule 1 stops resolving, and does it fail closed as the spec claims?
Concurrency (dossier 9.6): two tool calls firing POST at once both read HEAD state before either writes, and both emit. A per-invocation guard cannot see this.

value.topic: Codex hook installation (TOML + sha256 trust state)
value.why: Deferred from the matrix. Trust-state keys embed positional indices that go stale, and whether git-ai's trust hash matches what Codex computes could not be resolved from the source.
value.key_questions: Does Codex default async/timeout the way git-ai's hash assumes? What repairs a stale positional index? Is config.toml or hooks.json the right target?

value.effect: Every Key Finding and both design decisions trace to it; carries the five measured dead ends and the POC inventory.
AUTHORITATIVE for Phase 2 — the four write strategies, the per-agent matrix, and the four git-ai behaviours we deliberately do not reproduce.
16 working artifacts including the proven hook, the standalone tickler, and the negative-control prompts.

value.notes: Two design questions were put to the human and answered: follow git-ai and write an absolute binary path; Node startup cost is a watch-item, not a constraint.

Passes with a NARROW deviation, restated against the rule as written. architecture.md:137 forbids exit 0 for an UNCONFIGURED/UNBUILT verb; constitution P5 maps unconfigured->2, P6 maps error->1. architecture.md:91 ALREADY maps degraded->0, so a fire that reaches the socket and fails is `degraded` and needs NO deviation at all. The deviation is therefore scoped to `error` and `unconfigured` only, where a hook runtime must still exit 0 because its exit code is consumed by the customer's agent and a non-zero breaks their editor. The compensating control is now an acceptance criterion rather than a promise: a failed emit must be visible in `harness hooks status --json`.

Ports and adapters holds, but the runtime needs a NEW socket port — services must not import node:net directly (no-direct-node-io guards 188 service files). Core verb, not a repo extension: hooks are machine-scoped like telemetry and doctor must call it; P10 forbids a closed verb union, not core verbs.
docs/adr/ does not exist in this repo.
Domain mode off (HARNESS_DOMAINS unset, no docs/domains).

sections.name: implementation_summary
sections.value: Three phases. Phase 1 builds the runtime that is already proven — `harness hooks fire`, the HEAD-parent commit intercept, and the six-event trace2 tickler — behind ports, with the dangerous false-positive cases attacked rather than merely tested. Phase 2 builds the installer from ONE declarative matrix over four write strategies (JSON merge, plugin file, script file, and TOML deferred), fixing the four things git-ai gets wrong: no backups, order-and-comment-destroying writes, a two-substring ownership test, and unquoted paths. Phase 3 wires it into doctor beside the pinned git-ai install and documents it. Codex (TOML + sha256 trust state) and the three IDE-level targets are explicitly out of the matrix.

value.finding: Cursor's sandbox refuses AF_UNIX connect() — EPERM on BOTH git-ai daemon sockets — so a sandboxed git commit never reaches the daemon and NO note is written at all. Not misattribution: total loss, including AI lines that were checkpointed correctly.
value.action: The defect the plan exists to fix. Reproduce it in CI without Cursor via GIT_TRACE2_EVENT pointed at a discarded path.

value.finding: The daemon control API has no 'a commit happened' request (verified at the v1.6.21 pin: ping, checkpoint.run, sync.family, status.family, telemetry.submit, cas.submit, notes.flush, snapshot.watermarks, bash_session.*, bash_hook_attempt.*, await, shutdown). trace2 is the ONLY ingress to the note writer.
value.action: The fix must speak trace2. Do not look for a politer API — it does not exist.

value.finding: A real git commit trace2 stream carries NO sha; the daemon resolves the transition from a reflog cursor it already holds (ingestion spec ownership rule 1). It does not need the real stream — only to be told a commit command ran in repo X.
value.action: Six synthetic events suffice against the v1.6.21 pin on macOS — THREE RUNS OF THE SAME PAYLOAD on one machine, one daemon, one pin, of which one carried a paired negative control. Independent invocations, not independent implementations.

value.finding: The hook runner is NOT sandboxed (CURSOR_SANDBOX unset, both sockets reachable) while the agent shell is. The entire design rests on this, and it is measured on macOS only.
value.action: Verify on Linux in Phase 1 and hand Windows to the remote agent. Treat as an assumption until measured, never as a fact.

value.finding: git-ai takes NO backups anywhere (exhaustive grep, zero matches) and only ONE of its fifteen writers preserves comments. serde_json is declared without preserve_order, so every install alphabetically re-sorts the user's whole settings file.
value.action: Back up before first write; use comment- and order-preserving writes everywhere. This is the main thing we do differently.

value.finding: git-ai's ownership predicate is cmd.contains('git-ai') && cmd.contains('checkpoint'), used bare by four installers — so uninstall silently deletes any user hook whose command mentions both words.
value.action: Match on an explicit marker we own. Never a substring heuristic over someone else's command.

value.finding: Emitting a commit event when no commit happened could make the daemon claim an unrelated reflog entry — a FALSE note, worse than a missing one.
value.action: Detect by HEAD-parent equality, never by matching text in the command. Attack this case deliberately.

value.finding: Seven git-ai installers interpolate an UNQUOTED binary path into a shell string, and only three call normalize_windows_path_for_shell. A path containing a space produces a broken hook.
value.action: Always quote and always normalise, for every agent.

value.finding: Three git-ai installers (amp, opencode, pi) test a RELATIVE marker path, making detection cwd-dependent.
value.action: Absolute markers only, and status reports evidence rather than belief.

value.finding: Agents write compound && chains unprompted, which defeats Cursor terminal allowlisting — git was already allowlisted and the commit still ran sandboxed.
value.action: Never rely on or recommend an allowlist as a remedy.

value.finding: MEASURED on this machine 2026-08-09: the live ~/.cursor/hooks.json points at scratch/attrib-probe/*.mjs inside the MAIN checkout. scratch/ is untracked working space, so a cleanup silently turns every Cursor tool call into a failing command against a missing file — and nothing reports it, because hook failures are exit-0 by design. A hook whose target has been deleted is indistinguishable, from the customer side, from a hook that works.
value.action: The installer MUST write an absolute, QUOTED path to a STABLE installed binary, never a source or scratch path. And `harness hooks status` must PROVE the configured target still resolves (stat it) rather than reporting that a config entry exists — otherwise we reintroduce this plan's own silent-failure class from the installer side. Phase 2 turns this into a done_when assertion.

value.finding: We ALREADY have an agent-config backup mechanism: harness/cli/src/services/doctor/collector/backup.ts (from the #108 doctor work) writes ~/.git-ai/harness-backups/<iso>/ and was observed on this machine holding six real configs (.claude settings, .codex config, .copilot config, .cursor cli-config, .cursor hooks.json, .factory settings). It already reports copied / failed / UNDECLARED, the last distinguishing nothing-to-copy from we-did-not-know-where-to-look. NOTE: the directory name starts with harness- and lives under ~/.git-ai/, so it reads at a glance as git-ai's own — it is not. The workshop finding that git-ai takes no backups anywhere STANDS.
value.action: Phase 2 REUSES backupAgentConfigs rather than writing a second backup path. Two mechanisms writing agent-config backups to near-identical locations would make restore ambiguous — exactly the failure the uninstall-restores-original-bytes criterion exists to prevent.

value.finding: MEASURED end to end 2026-08-10 against the live daemon (git-ai 1.6.21, pid 81262): a commit made with trace2 DISCARDED gains NO note; our six synthetic events in ONE send produce a correct note in ~400ms. The note attributes a.txt lines 1-3 to tool github-copilot-cli with the running session id and human_author Jordan Knight. Identity was asserted three ways that agree with each other — file, line range, and the session id from the range line CROSS-REFERENCED against the sessions map in the note body — never a note count. A CAUSATION CONTROL was added unprompted: the identical repo and identical commit with NO emit leaves the note ABSENT over a window 25x longer than the measured arrival. This machine runs a live daemon with git-ai hooks installed, so ambient activity was a real alternative explanation and is now excluded.
value.action: ac-0001 and ac-0002 are MEASURED-on-macOS-against-a-live-daemon and UNVERIFIED-in-CI (no daemon there, and GIT_TRACE2_EVENT=0 is set run-wide). State it that way — SKIPPED and unproven are different claims. It also OBSERVES what the earlier over-emit key finding left unmeasured: line-level attribution comes from git-ai's own checkpoint records, and our events only tell it a commit happened.

value.risk: A wrong emit makes the daemon attribute an unrelated reflog entry, producing a confident false note.
value.mitigation: HEAD-parent guard; deliberate provocation tests (checkout, reset, rebase, amend, double-commit, no-op); stay silent whenever the transition is not exactly one new commit.

value.risk: The hook runner is sandboxed on Windows or Linux, invalidating the mechanism there.
value.mitigation: Measure on Linux in Phase 1. Ship Windows as UNVERIFIED rather than assumed; the remote agent is the only instrument.

value.risk: Writing into a shared agent config destroys another tool's entries, or silently re-sorts and de-comments the user's file.
value.mitigation: Comment- and order-preserving writes; back up before first write; fixture tests that install with git-ai's own entries present and assert they survive byte-identical.

value.risk: Our uninstall leaves debris, as every git-ai uninstall does.
value.mitigation: Uninstall symmetry is a test: install then uninstall must return the file to its ORIGINAL bytes.

value.risk: git-ai changes the socket path, the pipe-name digest, or the trace2 event shape in a later version.
value.mitigation: Pin, and carry one MEASURED_AGAINST_PIN constant whose drift from the live version is reported at runtime rather than failing silently.

value.risk: Node process startup on every tool call adds latency (two invocations per tool use).
value.mitigation: Exit before loading anything on tool names that cannot be commit-bearing. Watch-item, not a gate — harness already runs many times a session.

value.risk: An absolute binary path in the customer config breaks when npm relocates the binary on upgrade.
value.mitigation: Follow git-ai (decided). harness hooks status detects a path that no longer resolves; doctor reports it.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Never emit unless the agent AUTHORED the commit here. HEAD advancing by one whose first parent is the recorded HEAD is NOT sufficient — SEVEN transitions satisfy it byte-identically (merge --squash, cherry-pick -n, revert -n, git apply, checkout REF -- path, restore --source, read-tree -m -u). The discriminator is the INDEX STATE recorded at PRE: a genuine agent edit leaves a CLEAN index, every defeater leaves an ALREADY-STAGED one. `.git` state does not exist at decision time — SQUASH_MSG is unlinked before even git's own post-commit hook runs. A human committing inside the PRE/POST bracket is indistinguishable and is a KNOWN, ACCEPTED blind spot. When in doubt, stay silent.

Every hook code path exits 0 and writes nothing the agent can see. A broken harness must never break the customer's editor session. This is a DELIBERATE deviation from the exit-code anti-pattern (gate G2) and failures must surface through `harness hooks status` instead.
Back up any config file before our first write to it, and name the backup in the output. git-ai takes none; that is the gap we are closing.
Preserve comments and key order in every file we touch. Never re-serialize a user's config wholesale.
Match only on a marker we own. Never claim or delete a hook entry using a substring heuristic over someone else's command.
Refuse to overwrite an unmanaged file rather than clobbering it (git-ai's Cline installer is the model; its Amp installer is the counter-example).
Assert on note IDENTITY per commit, never on a note COUNT — the count moves for unrelated reasons.
Measure behaviour against the PINNED git-ai version, never the ~/github/git-ai checkout HEAD.
Do not retry the five measured dead ends in dossier section 6.
Never recommend that a customer weaken their sandbox; networkPolicy default allow opens ALL egress and is not a remedy we ship.
